newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma removes blockades around Suu Kyi's house.
newsitem.headline: Burma removes blockades around Suu Kyi's house.

text.p: Burma's military government on Monday removed the blockades barring access to the road leading to democracy leader Aung San Suu Kyi's house, witnesses said.
They said the barricades, which had been manned by heavily armed soldiers for 10 days, were removed late on Monday afternoon.
The ruling military body, the State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC), said it set up the barricades to prevent unrest.

The blockades prevented the Nobel Peace laureate from holding regular weekend speeches to supporters for the fourth weekend in a row. They were also in place from September 26 to October 8 to stop Suu Kyi's National League for Democracy party from holding a party congress in late September.
Diplomats expect the SLORC will continue to put up the blockades at weekends to prevent the speeches outside Suu Kyi's house.
The SLORC has said the gatherings are illegal but Suu Kyi has vowed to hold them.
